BiblicalUsage: Zed names the arrogant person, the one who acts with pride and scorn toward God and toward others. Proverbs defines him plainly, that the proud and haughty scorner deals in proud wrath, and the Psalmist says God rebukes the proud who stray from His commandments. Malachi warns that the day is coming when all the proud will burn like stubble, and Isaiah says God will punish the world for its evil and lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe pride is the root sin, the one that makes a person unteachable and God unneeded. Scripture never treats it as a small flaw; it treats it as rebellion wearing good clothes. My position is that God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble, and the only safe answer to pride is to fall on that grace before the day Malachi describes arrives.
